query: In conventional alloys, loss of toughness has long been associated with grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation. By contrast, compositionally complex high-entropy alloys can suppress rapid grain coarsening and deleterious intermetallic formation and have shown favorable strength–ductility combinations and resistance to high-temperature softening and low-temperature embrittlement. These findings do not establish what governs possible toughness degradation in an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy. Under the constraint of retaining a compositionally complex alloy suitable for demanding engineering service, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains whether and why brittle behavior emerges? Specify a controlled comparison that would distinguish the hypothesis from conventional-alloy expectations, predicted observations relative to the initial baseline, its service and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification outcome.

generation.hypothesis: Under service‐relevant thermal and mechanical loading, an initially homogeneous single‐phase high-entropy alloy develops local compositional fluctuations at grain boundaries that lead to the nucleation of nanoscale, less-coherent precipitates. These emergent grain-boundary features reduce intergranular cohesion and promote brittle fracture, a mechanism distinct from the conventional segregation-driven embrittlement seen in traditional alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: A single-phase, compositionally complex HEA (e.g., equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi) with a uniform microstructure and high toughness.
generation.intervention: Subject samples to controlled high-temperature aging (e.g., 700–900 °C) combined with cyclic or static mechanical loading over extended durations reflective of service conditions.
generation.conditions: Aging and mechanical testing under temperatures near the upper service limit, with cyclic loading or hold at high stress to promote local diffusion, while a control group is maintained in the as-processed state.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of nanoscale grain-boundary precipitates or localized elemental segregations that alter the cohesion of the grain boundary (e.g., slight enrichment of elements that form brittle intermetallic compounds).
generation.mechanism: Elevated temperature and mechanical stresses induce enhanced atomic mobility at grain boundaries. This facilitates localized compositional fluctuations that nucleate incoherent (or less coherent) precipitates. These features hinder grain-boundary sliding and absorb less plastic strain, thus serving as crack initiation sites under load, ultimately degrading toughness.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the unaged, as-processed baseline, the aged and loaded HEA will exhibit reduced ductility and a transition to intergranular brittle fracture, with microstructural characterization revealing new grain-boundary precipitates or segregation patterns.
generation.baseline: The as-processed, uniformly tough single-phase HEA with no detectable grain-boundary precipitates or compositional gradients.
generation.boundary: This effect is expected under service conditions where temperatures and stress levels are high enough to activate local diffusion but remain below the threshold for full phase transformation or catastrophic grain coarsening.
generation.uncertainty: The exact kinetics of elemental segregation and the corresponding critical temperature-stress-time combination necessary to trigger the formation of detrimental grain-boundary features remain to be quantitatively determined.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of identical single-phase HEA specimens. Subject one set to prolonged aging at 700–900 °C under cyclic or sustained load that simulates service conditions, while maintaining the other set as an as-processed control. After aging, perform standardized tensile and fracture toughness tests, and conduct microstructural analysis (using TEM/SEM with EDS) focusing on grain-boundary chemistry and the presence of nanoscale precipitates.
measurements: Fracture toughness and crack propagation mode (intergranular versus transgranular)
Quantitative TEM/SEM EDS mapping of grain-boundary regions for precipitate formation or compositional variations
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the aged specimens do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in ductility/toughness relative to the control, or if microstructural analysis fails to detect any notable grain-boundary precipitate formation or segregation, then the hypothesis that service conditions induce a precipitation-driven embrittlement in HEAs will be falsified.

Question: How can the compressive strength of the NbMoCrTiAl refractory high-entropy alloy be improved for high-temperature structural applications while maintaining oxidation resistance?. System: NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy matrix with in-situ formed TiC and Al2O3 reinforcement particles.
